issues.description: Dataclass field ordering: required `service` field added to subclass of ControlFrame/Frame which has default-valued fields
issues.detail: `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` adds `service: "FrameProcessor"` with no default. If any ancestor dataclass (`ControlFrame`/`Frame`) defines fields with defaults (typical for Frame base classes that have `id`, `name`, `pts`, `metadata` defaults), Python will raise `TypeError: non-default argument 'service' follows default argument` at class-definition time. The fact that tests pass suggests this may work, but it's fragile and depends on whether `ControlFrame`'s chain has any defaulted fields. Should use `field(default=None)` or `kw_only=True` to be safe.

issues.description: Frame carries a reference to a FrameProcessor — design smell and coupling concern
issues.detail: Frames are typically pure data payloads that flow through processors. Embedding a `FrameProcessor` instance inside a frame creates an unusual back-reference: frames now know about specific processor instances. This complicates serialization, logging (a processor's repr can be huge), equality, and debugging. An identifier (string name or id) would decouple this without losing targeting capability.

issues.description: Equality check uses `==` instead of `is` for FrameProcessor identity comparison
issues.detail: `if frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` compares processors via `==`. If `FrameProcessor` (or any ancestor dataclass) defines `__eq__` based on field values, two distinct processor instances with equal fields would compare equal and incorrectly suppress the frame. Identity comparison (`is`) more accurately expresses 'same processor instance' intent.

issues.description: Frame can leak downstream if active service changes between request and propagation
issues.detail: The new suppression logic only consumes the frame when `frame.service == active_service`. If `strategy.active_service` changes after the request is queued but before the frame propagates back through `push_frame`, the frame leaks out of the switcher into downstream processors that don't expect to see internal `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame`s. The previous code unconditionally suppressed it, which was safer. Consider suppressing all `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame`s regardless of target, since by the time the frame reaches `push_frame` it has already been handled.

Renaming `RequestMetadataFrame` to `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` is a hard breaking change for any external code importing the old name. Standard practice is to provide a deprecation alias (`RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` with a `DeprecationWarning`) for at least one release. The changelog labels this `changed.md` but it's effectively a `removed`/`breaking` event.

issues.description: No test added for the new mismatched-service suppression behavior
issues.detail: The PR claims all 12 existing tests pass, but the new conditional suppression (`if frame.service == self.strategy.active_service`) has no dedicated test covering the case where `frame.service` is NOT the active service. Without that test, the new branch logic is unverified and a future refactor could regress it silently.

issues.description: Forward reference `"FrameProcessor"` is unresolved by typing.get_type_hints at runtime
issues.detail: The `service: "FrameProcessor"` annotation uses a string forward reference but `FrameProcessor` is never imported into `frames.py`. Dataclasses don't resolve this at runtime, so it works for instantiation — but any caller using `typing.get_type_hints(ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame)` (common in serialization, validators, documentation tools) will raise `NameError`. Consider a `TYPE_CHECKING` guarded import for cleanliness.

issues.description: Docstring on push_frame no longer describes the leak edge case
issues.detail: The updated docstring says the frame is suppressed when targeting the active service but does not explain what happens when `frame.service != active_service`. Readers will reasonably assume it's always suppressed; documenting the gap (or closing it) would help future maintainers.

issues.description: Ordering change in STTService.process_frame: metadata pushed before the request frame
issues.detail: Previously `RequestMetadataFrame` was silently consumed and only `_push_stt_metadata()` was emitted. Now `_push_stt_metadata()` runs first, then the original request frame is pushed downstream. Downstream consumers will now see `STTMetadataFrame` followed by `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame`. If any downstream processor reacts to the request frame, it will see the metadata before the request — verify this ordering is intended and documented.

dissents.topic: Should the frame carry a FrameProcessor reference or a service identifier?

positions.position: Holding a FrameProcessor reference is fine because the frame is internal to the switcher's queue→handler→push cycle and never crosses serialization boundaries. Identity comparison is fast and unambiguous. Renaming/refactoring later is cheap.

Frames are data envelopes flowing across processor boundaries. Embedding a live processor reference inverts the dependency direction and couples the frame type to the processor lifecycle. A string name or stable id keeps frames as pure data and avoids subtle leakage of internal handles into logs, traces, or future serialization paths.

dissents.topic: Should ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame leak downstream when target != active_service?

positions.position: Internal control frames should never escape the component that owns them. The switcher introduced this frame; it should unconditionally suppress it in `push_frame` to maintain encapsulation. The targeting check belongs only on the receiving side (services deciding whether to act).

Only the targeted service handles the frame; non-targeted services in a ParallelPipeline branch may still need to forward it to find their target. Conditional suppression based on whether the frame reached the active service is a deliberate signal that the right service consumed it.

dissents.topic: Is the rename a breaking change worth a deprecation alias?

positions.position: `RequestMetadataFrame` was likely an internal control frame for ServiceSwitcher; few external users import it. A clean rename with a changelog entry is sufficient and avoids carrying dead aliases forever.

It was exported from `pipecat.frames.frames`, which is a public module. Any external integration importing the old name silently breaks at import time on upgrade. A one-release deprecation alias with a warning costs nothing and protects downstream users.

review.summary: The PR is a focused, well-scoped rename that adds service targeting to an internal control frame. The core change is sensible and the existing test suite is updated consistently. However, several issues warrant attention before merge: the new required `service` field on a dataclass that inherits from frames with defaulted fields is fragile (P1); embedding a `FrameProcessor` reference inside a Frame is a design smell when a stable identifier would suffice (P1); the equality check should likely be identity (`is`) to avoid false positives from dataclass `__eq__` (P1); the conditional suppression in `push_frame` introduces a real leak path if `active_service` changes mid-flight, where the previous code was unconditionally safe (P1); and the rename is a breaking public-API change without a deprecation alias (P1). Tests are not extended to cover the new conditional suppression branch.
